memory_candidates.content: A `set +e` / `set -e` toggle placed inside a bash FUNCTION to bracket one risky command leaks: `set -e`/`set +e` are GLOBAL shell attributes, not function-scoped, so if the enclosing script never otherwise uses `-e` (e.g. it runs under `set -uo pipefail` only, a common convention in this repo's scripts), turning `-e` ON inside the function silently activates errexit for the REST of the script after that function returns -- including any later code whose legitimate design relies on inspecting a non-zero exit status from a plain pipeline (e.g. a `grep -qF ... ; if [ $? ...]` idiom, or a bare `var="$(cmd | grep ... )"` assignment where the pipeline's expected-to-sometimes-fail exit code should NOT abort the script). The bug manifests as a silent, no-error-message, unexpected script termination -- `bash -x` tracing is required to see it (the trace simply stops after the risky command's line, no further output). Fix: don't toggle `-e` at all if the script doesn't otherwise use it; just capture `$?` directly (`cmd; rc=$?`) without any `set +e`/`set -e` bracketing.

Under `set -u`, combining multiple assignments on ONE `local` statement where a later variable's value expression references an earlier variable from the SAME statement (e.g. `local name="$1" dir="$WORKDIR/repo-$name"`) fails with an 'unbound variable' error on the second variable. Bash expands all the word values for a compound `local a=X b=Y` command before the `local` builtin declares/assigns any of them, so `$name` in the second word is evaluated against whatever `name` was BEFORE this statement ran (typically unset), not the `$1` just assigned in the same statement. Fix: split into separate `local` statements, one per line, when a later variable's value depends on an earlier one declared in the same group.

In this repo's extension manifest.json schema, the `provides.scripts` deploy category (`entry_kind = "file"` in lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/loader.lua) copies each listed entry as an individual flat FILE from `scripts/<entry>` to `.claude/scripts/<entry>` -- there is no directory-glob or recursive-directory support for this category. A test fixture TREE (e.g. `scripts/tests/fixtures/<name>/*`) must be listed as one explicit manifest entry PER FILE, not as a single directory path, or the untracked files are silently never deployed. The literature extension's manifest.json already demonstrates this precedent (`tests/fixtures/tier3-*.json` listed individually); a new extension adding fixture files should follow the same pattern rather than assuming a directory entry works.
